title: Affine charts for restriction of scalars
statement: Let $p:S'\to S$ be a finite locally free morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $V\subseteq S$ be an affine open subscheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], and let $q:U\to S'$ be a morphism with $U$ affine such that $p\circ q$ factors through $V$. For a $V$-scheme $T$, set $H(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{S'}(T\times_S S',U)$, with restriction by precomposition [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is an affine $V$-scheme $R$ with bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_V(T,R)\simeq H(T)$ natural in every $V$-scheme $T$. Neither finite type nor finite presentation of $U\to S'$ is assumed; zero and varying rank of $p$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0BL3 (lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine), with the polynomial-coefficient construction in Tag 05Y6 (lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine), imposing the equations that a morphism is over S prime. This is the affine case explicitly proved in BLR 7.6 Theorem 4, printed p.194; local BLR PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $Z=V\times_S S'$ and let $q_V:U\to Z$ have components $U\to V$ and $q$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $T\times_V Z$ with $T\times_S S'$ for every $V$-scheme $T$, compatibly with both projections and all maps of tests. The map $p_V:Z\to V$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by the respective base-change statements, hence finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. In particular $Z$ is affine since $V$ is affine. Also $U\to V$ is affine: in [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] use the one-member affine cover $\{V\}$, whose inverse image is the assumed affine scheme $U$.

source.place: Tags 02KB (lemma-finite-flat), 02KD (lemma-base-change-finite-locally-free), and 01S8 (lemma-characterize-affine); explicit restriction of the base.

proof.text: Choose an affine open cover $(W_i)$ of $V$ for which $Z_i=Z\times_V W_i$ has finite free coordinate algebra over $W_i$. Here is the required variable-rank justification: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant] decomposes $V$ into open-and-closed rank loci. Cover these loci by affine opens $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; their inverse images in $Z$ are affine by finiteness. Their morphisms are still finite locally free by the same base-change facts as in Step 1, and of constant degree $d$ over an $A$ contained in the locus $V_d$ of degree $d$, since each fibre over a point of $A$ is the fibre of $Z\to V$ there. On each such affine $A$, [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-principal-basis-cover] gives principal opens $D(f)$ on which the coordinate algebra has a finite basis, including rank zero; each $D(f)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]. Use all these principal opens as the $W_i$. Put $U_i=U\times_V W_i$, affine by base change of the affine map $U\to V$ and affineness of $W_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BL3 (lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine), choice of finite-free base charts; Tags 04MH and 02KB in morphisms.tex expanded by existing basis-cover statement.

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-affine-finite-free-hom] twice, with ambient base $W_i$, finite-free source $Z_i$, and targets $U_i$ and $Z_i$. Fixing the structural map of each test gives affine $W_i$-schemes $M_i,N_i$ representing respectively $G_i(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{W_i}(T\times_{W_i}Z_i,U_i)$ and $E_i(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{W_i}(T\times_{W_i}Z_i,Z_i)$, naturally for all $W_i$-schemes $T$. Postcomposition with $q_i:U_i\to Z_i$ is a natural map $G_i\to E_i$, hence by the Yoneda bijection gives $a_i:M_i\to N_i$. The projection $T\times_{W_i}Z_i\to Z_i$ is natural in $T$ and gives $e_i:W_i\to N_i$. Concretely $a_i$ corresponds to $q_i$ composed with the universal map of $M_i$, and $e_i$ corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_{Z_i}$. Yoneda naturality says that their values on any test are exactly these postcomposition and projection formulas.

source.place: Tag 05Y6 (lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine); two applications and the explicit relative-condition construction.

proof.text: Form $R_i=M_i\times_{a_i,N_i,e_i}W_i$. A map $T\to R_i$ over $W_i$ is exactly a map $f:T\to M_i$ over $W_i$ with $a_i f=e_i t$, where $t:T\to W_i$ is the structural map. Under Step 3 this equality is $q_i b=\operatorname{pr}_{Z_i}$ for the corresponding $b:T\times_{W_i}Z_i\to U_i$. Thus $b$ is precisely a $Z_i$-morphism, equivalently an $S'$-morphism: both its components to $W_i$ already agree, and equality to $Z_i=W_i\times_S S'$ is equality of the two projections. Factoring a map into $U_i=U\times_V W_i$ is equally the pair consisting of its map to $U$ and the prescribed map to $W_i$. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_i}(T,R_i)\simeq H(T)$ naturally on all $W_i$-schemes. Each operation is composition or the unique map with specified projections; it therefore commutes with precomposition by every map of tests.

source.place: Relative equation supplement to Tag 0BL3: fibre-product universal property imposes the S-prime condition without any separation assumption.

proof.text: The scheme $R_i$ is affine. Indeed $M_i,N_i$ are affine by Step 3, so [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] applied to the single affine open $N_i$ shows that $a_i:M_i\to N_i$ is affine. Its base change $R_i\to W_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1); its source is affine by (2), since $W_i$ is affine. This argument imposes neither a closed-diagonal condition on $S'$ nor finiteness conditions on $U_i$.

source.place: Tags 01S8 (lemma-characterize-affine) and 01SD (lemma-base-change-affine): affineness of the relative-condition fibre.

proof.text: On $W_{ij}=W_i\cap W_j$, the schemes $R_i\times_V W_{ij}$ and $R_j\times_V W_{ij}$ both represent $H$ restricted to $W_{ij}$-schemes. The pullback universal property identifies their point sets with the respective point sets of Step 4; that step applies to all test schemes, so $W_{ij}$ need not be affine. The identity transformation of $H$ therefore gives a unique isomorphism $\varphi_{ij}$ between them by [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection]. The reverse transformation supplies the inverse. On a triple intersection both $\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}$ and $\varphi_{ik}$ induce the identity of $H$; Yoneda injectivity gives their equality. The diagonal transition is likewise the identity. Apply [lem-galois-glue] to this Zariski cover of $V$ to obtain a $V$-scheme $R$ and compatible identifications $R\times_V W_i\simeq R_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BL3 (lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine), base-chart gluing; schemes.tex Tags 01JB (lemma-glue) and 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes) via existing relative gluing theorem.

proof.text: For any $T\to V$, let $T_i=T\times_V W_i$, the inverse-image open subschemes of $T$. They cover $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. A map $b:T\times_S S'\to U$ over $S'$ restricts on each $T_i$ to an element of $H(T_i)$, hence gives a unique map $f_i:T_i\to R_i\to R$. The compatibility in Step 6 shows these maps agree on $T_i\cap T_j$. Morphism gluing gives a unique $f:T\to R$, over $V$ since its composite to $V$ agrees with that of $T$ on the cover. Conversely restrict $f$ to the $T_i$ and use Step 4. The resulting maps to $U$ glue on the inverse-image open cover of $T\times_S S'$; their composites to $S'$ agree with the projection there, so they agree globally. These operations are inverse by gluing uniqueness. Pulling back along any $T'\to T$ gives the same local maps on the pulled-back cover by Step 4; uniqueness proves the required global naturality.

source.place: Tag 01JA (section-glueing-schemes), morphism gluing as in Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), and Tag 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product); all-test naturality in the gluing argument of Tag 0BL3.

proof.text: The inverse images of the affine cover $(W_i)$ under $R\to V$ are $R_i$, hence affine by Step 5. Therefore [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] makes $R\to V$ affine, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2) makes $R$ affine since $V$ is affine. This proves all clauses. No step required finite generation of a target coordinate algebra; the two finite-free Hom applications explicitly allow arbitrary algebras. On a rank-zero chart the same Hom theorem gives singleton point sets for both $G_i$ and $E_i$, so their representatives and their fibre represent the terminal functor and $R_i\simeq W_i$. Empty bases and empty tests are included by the same universal properties and morphism-gluing uniqueness. The rank decomposition in Step 2 allows different ranks on different components.

source.place: Tag 0BL3 (lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-into-affine), affineness after gluing; rank-zero and unrestricted-presentation cases from Tag 05Y6.
